Error.description:
Standard error envelope. **Wire shape note (applies to every
error response in this spec):** GoFr nests the handler's error
object under a top-level `"error"` key, and the human-readable
text travels in a field named `"error"` — NOT `"message"`
(`apiErr.Response()` in `internal/httpapi/types.go`). The actual
bytes on the wire are:

    {"error": {"code": "<slug>", "error": "<human text>"}}

The `message` property below is the *logical* hint field; read it
from `error.error` when consuming raw HTTP. Extra sibling fields
(e.g. the 412 precondition envelopes' `mfa_challenge_token`,
`revocation_token`, `active_sessions`, `tenant_id`) are nested
under the same top-level `"error"` object.

`code` is a stable machine-readable
slug; `message` is a human-readable hint. Common 401 codes
emitted by the auth surface:

- `invalid_credentials` — bad password / token / OTP.
- `invalid_audience` — id-token `aud` not registered (ADR-046).
- `invalid_token` — malformed / expired bearer.
- `wrong_scope` — bearer present but wrong class
  (e.g. user JWT where platform is required).
- `bff_bearer_required` — every zone requires the BFF escort (ADR-088)
  and the inbound platform bearer is missing. Emitted on
  `POST /auth/token` + `POST /auth/logout`. NOTE: `POST /auth/login`
  requires a platform bearer **unconditionally** (ADR-047 §2 — it
  gates via the platform-token check, which runs *before* the BFF
  gate), so a **bearerless `/auth/login` returns `401 unauthorized`
  ("missing bearer"), never `bff_bearer_required`**. The
  `bff_bearer_required` code is only reachable on
  `/auth/token` / `/auth/logout`.
- `key_class_mismatch` — declared `grant_type` on
  `/auth/login` (`api_key` vs `platform_api_key`) doesn't
  match the api-key's class (ADR-051).
- `user_not_invited` — known user but not a member of any
  tenant in the resolved zone. (Returned as **403**, not 401 —
  listed here for discoverability.)
- `escort_suspended` — **403**, not 401 (listed here for
  discoverability): the `/auth/*` escort (the platform bearer the
  partner's BFF presents) is refused because the account it was
  minted for is suspended or deactivated (ADR-104 R-d). Distinct from
  `user_suspended`, which names the END USER's row; this one means
  the partner's own escort credential has to be replaced.
- `refresh_invalid` — on `POST /auth/token` only: the presented
  refresh token is expired, revoked, or reuse-detected. Terminal
  for the caller — re-authentication is required (no retry helps).

LoginRequest.description:
ADR-051 (v0.7.0): `/auth/login` is the single
credential-exchange endpoint. The body's `grant_type`
discriminates which credentials are presented and which
subject class the issued tokens carry.

Inbound bearer rules (the handler dispatches on `grant_type`
before applying any bearer gate):

- `provider_token`, `password`, `otp` — **user
  grants**. Require `Authorization: Bearer <platform access
  token>` (the zone's BFF / partner-backend gate, ADR-041 +
  ADR-047). Zone is resolved from the bearer's `zone_id`
  claim; body `zone_id` is ignored.
- `api_key`, `platform_api_key` — **api-key grants**.
  Unauthenticated; the raw API key travels in the body. Any
  inbound bearer is rejected. The api-key's class must match
  the declared `grant_type`; mismatch → 401
  `key_class_mismatch`.

The legacy `method` selector (pre-ADR-051) is **removed** at
its announced `Sunset: 2026-08-01`. A body carrying only
`method` now 400s `missing_grant_type`; send `grant_type`
(+ `provider` for `provider_token`). `grant_type=password` is
**IMPLEMENTED as of ADR-104** — it filled the ADR-042 slot and no
longer 400s `unknown_method`.

ADR-046 (still applies under `provider_token`/`google`):
`tenant_id` is required on tenant-scoped origins so the
verifier can pick the tenant's per-tenant `client_id`s (plus
the platform-default list) to validate `aud`. On zone-root
origins (e.g. `example.test` or a platform's admin
console apex) discovery returns `tenant_id: null` and the
field is OPTIONAL — zone-scoped `identity_providers`
client_ids gate the sign-in instead (issuer v0.27.2).

custom_claims.description:
Optional partner-supplied claims, gated by
`zones.config.access_token_custom_claim_keys`
(SDK SPEC §4.2). Only meaningful on user grants when an
access token is minted on the first call (single-tenant,
no MFA). Otherwise pass on `POST /auth/token`.

role_permissions.description:
**ADR-100 D16 — the narrowing operand for a user-API-key token.**
The permissions the holder's ROLE confers, in YOUR vocabulary, used
to narrow that token's `permissions_cap` claim to THIS org.

Supply it from your own role -> permission map. ZoneID stores no
partner catalog and will not resolve it for you (D17): the strings
are opaque here, and the issuer does not fall back to
`zone_roles.permissions` even for `aud=zoneid`, so the claim stays
a pure function of the request.

**Caller-ASSERTED and unverified**, audited as such — the convention
`source_org_id` already uses. That is safe for a stated reason, not
by assumption: the claim minted is
`stored_cap INTERSECT role_permissions`, and `A INTERSECT B` is a
subset of `A` for every `B`, so a wrong or hostile list can only
NARROW, never widen past the stored cap. Worst case is exactly the
pre-ADR-100 behaviour.

**OPTIONAL. Omitted / `null` = not supplied** — the stored cap
travels unnarrowed (D6), which keeps every existing caller working.
**An empty array is NOT the same thing**: it says "this role confers
nothing here" and produces a `403` (below).

**Ignored for an UNCAPPED key** (D7), whose claim stays absent
whatever you send — uncapped is delivered by omission and that
mechanism does not change. Ignored, too, for any token that is not
key-derived: there is no cap to intersect with.

⚠️ **An empty INTERSECTION is `403 no_permissions_in_org`, never an
empty claim** (D8). The two are indistinguishable to a reader of the
token, and `[]` on the claim side already means "capped to nothing",
which the issuer must never emit. The narrowing is **per-org**, so a
multi-org key mints in one org and is refused in another — the error
names the org, or it reads as "the key is broken".

LoginRequestAPIKey.description:
Service api-key exchange. **No inbound bearer** — the raw
API key travels in `api_key`. The key must have been issued
as a service key; if it was issued as a platform key the
server returns 401 `key_class_mismatch`.

LoginRequestOTP.description:
OTP login (ADR-071; direct cutover from the former
`otp` grant). Under ADR-071 this authenticates a
**service account** (`users.kind=service`) via a `view_bff` OTP
an owner/admin minted for it (`POST /auth/otp/issue`
`purpose=login`). The `kind × mode` gate rejects a `kind=human`
subject here (humans elevate via TOTP, never an owner-minted OTP)
— failure collapses to `invalid_credentials` (no enumeration).
Gated by `zones.config.otp_login_enabled`. Inbound bearer:
platform access JWT.

identifier.description:
The service account's login handle (email/phone). Resolved
against the zone's user lookup. Failure → `invalid_credentials`
(no enumeration).

presented.description: The OTP value minted for the service account.

LoginRequestPassword.description:
**ADR-104 — native username/password, tenant-scoped.** Fills the
ADR-042 u/p slot, which was reserved on the wire and unimplemented
until this release. Inbound bearer: platform access JWT.

Credentials are Argon2id (issuer-side; no SDK ever hashes a password).
A `kind=service` account may NOT hold one — its lane is `api_key` and
`otp`/`view_bff` (ADR-071); a service account with a human-chosen
secret is a shared password by another name.

Every existing gate applies and none is added: MFA floors
(ADR-059/075), Kind x Method and App x Method eligibility (ADR-072),
`login_attempts` rate limiting, session classes, ADR-004's tenant lock.

identifier.description:
Identifier the user logs in with — email, E.164 phone, or
**username** (ADR-104). Resolution failure surfaces as
`invalid_credentials` (no enumeration).

The identifier is CLASSIFIED ONCE, never tried as several kinds in
turn: contains `@` -> email; matches E.164 -> phone; matches the
username grammar -> username; otherwise the login fails having
queried nothing. A fallthrough would make a string that is a valid
username AND a valid something-else resolve differently depending
on which store answered first — a nondeterministic identity.

**Username grammar** (case-FOLDED, 3-32 chars):
`^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]{1,30})[a-z0-9]$`. No `@`, no `+`, not
all-digits — the three classes are disjoint by construction. There
is no per-zone username policy knob.

new_password.description:
**Change at sign-in (ADR-104 § Amendment 2026-10-09, R14-R21; spec
`0.53.0`).** Send it ONLY after a login answered
`403 password_must_change` — the credential was set by an
administrator and must be replaced before it authenticates. One
call then replaces the password and signs in.

- Validated as input before anything else, and never counted by the
  per-identifier throttle: `400 password_too_short` (< 12 bytes),
  `400 password_too_long` (> 1024), `400 password_unchanged` (equal
  to `presented`). An empty string is treated as absent.
- `presented` wrong: `401 invalid_credentials`, as without this
  field; nothing is stored.
- Sent when the credential is NOT must-change:
  `400 password_change_not_required`, decided only after
  `presented` verifies. Nothing changes and no session is created;
  change a self-chosen password with `PUT /me/password`.
- Identifier throttled: `429 login_throttled`; nothing changes.
- Success: the new password is stored, the obligation is cleared,
  EVERY other session of this membership is revoked, the holder is
  notified (ADR-079, no link, no code), and the response is an
  ordinary `200` login — MFA gates apply unchanged, so
  `tenants[].mfa_required` may still withhold the access token.
- A `5xx` after the password was stored leaves the NEW password in
  force: retry with `presented=<new>` and no `new_password`.

Ignored (with a `Warning: 299`) on every other `grant_type`.

presented.description:
The presented password. Minimum **12** bytes, maximum **1024**
(a KDF-cost bound, not a policy opinion). No composition rules.
When `new_password` is sent, this is the CURRENT password.

tenant_id.description:
Optional for email/phone — when set and the user is a member, the
response is single-tenant and an access token is minted on the
first call.

**Load-bearing for a USERNAME login.** Usernames are unique per
TENANT, not per zone (`alice` in two orgs is routinely two
people), so a username alone does not identify a principal. The
tenant is resolved as: this field if present, else the tenant
derived from the request's subdomain / `Origin`. **Explicit wins**,
including when the two disagree — a partner BFF is server-side and
its Origin is its own, not the end user's org, so an Origin-wins
rule would make BFF-fronted username login unimplementable without
one host per org.

This is a hint about WHERE TO LOOK, never about who the caller is:
the resolved user's own `tenant_id` governs everything downstream,
and the password still has to be right in that namespace.

Neither source yielding a tenant on a username login is
`400 tenant_required` — a NAMED code, not a generic credential
failure, because it is a caller-integration mistake rather than a
wrong password and the two must not look alike in your logs. It
leaks nothing: it is answerable before any identifier lookup runs.

LoginRequestPlatformAPIKey.description:
Platform api-key exchange (ADR-041 §1, §3). **No inbound
bearer** — the raw API key travels in `api_key`. The key
must have been issued as a platform key; if it was issued
as a service key the server returns 401
`key_class_mismatch`. The platform access token returned
here is what callers present as the inbound bearer for
the user-facing grants (`provider_token`, `password`,
`otp`).

LoginRequestProviderToken.description:
Exchange a third-party id-token (Google, Firebase phone
auth, etc.) for a ZoneID refresh token. Inbound bearer:
platform access JWT.

provider.description:
`google`, `firebase`, `microsoft`, `apple`, and `facebook`
have working direct OIDC verifiers. `firebase_phone` is a
legacy alias for the Firebase verifier. `facebook` accepts
only the OIDC ID-token ("Limited Login") flavor — the classic
access token is not supported (it needs an app secret ZoneID
does not store). `github` is post-v1 and listed so the schema
documents the forward roadmap. The accepted `aud` (client_id;
for `apple` the Services ID, for `facebook` the app id) is
resolved per zone/tenant from identity_providers; for
`firebase` the configured value is the Firebase project id.
`tenant_id` is optional for every provider on a zone-root
origin (e.g. example.test or a partner admin console),
where zone-scoped client_ids gate sign-in with no tenant pin.

tenant_id.description:
Optional. Pins membership resolution to one tenant; required
only when a partner end-user origin resolves to a specific
tenant and the response must be single-tenant. On a zone-root
origin it is absent — zone-scoped client_ids gate sign-in
(v0.27.2; ADR-046). When set, the response is single-tenant and
an access token is minted on the first call.

LoginRequestTokenExchange.description:
Workload identity federation exchange (ADR-057). **No inbound
bearer** — the partner workload's ambient OIDC token (GCP
metadata server or GitHub Actions) travels in `subject_token`.
The issuer validates it against the RI-pinned JWKS for its
issuer, enforces `aud` (the global RI audience) + `iat`-freshness
+ one-time-use, then selects the unique `federation_binding`
whose `match_claims` all hold and mints the **same**
`class="platform"` session the `platform_api_key` grant returns —
including ADR-089's shape: an access token with **no**
`refresh_token`. Re-mint by exchanging a fresh assertion.
401 on: unknown issuer, invalid/stale/replayed assertion, audience
mismatch, or no matching binding.

subject_token.description: The workload OIDC JWT (Google ID token or GitHub Actions OIDC token).

subject_token_type.description: Optional; defaults to the JWT token-type URN when omitted.

LoginResponse.description:
`/auth/login` response. Three success shapes. The shape is
selected by `subject_type` and, for users, by tenant
cardinality + MFA state:

1. **User, fully resolved** (`subject_type:"user"`,
   single-tenant, no MFA pending): refresh + access +
   tenant_id + role + expires_in + tenants[] + user.
2. **User, multi-tenant OR MFA pending**
   (`subject_type:"user"`): refresh + tenants[] + user;
   caller picks a tenant via `POST /auth/token`. No
   access_token / tenant_id / role / expires_in.
3. **Api-key grants** (`subject_type:"service"` |
   `"platform"` via `grant_type=api_key` /
   `platform_api_key`) and the token-exchange grant:
   access + expires_in + `"tenants": []` (present but always
   empty). **No `refresh_token`** — ADR-089: the credential
   itself is re-presentable, so a refresh token would be a
   weaker duplicate of one the caller already holds, and the
   field is omitted entirely. Re-mint by calling this
   endpoint again. No tenant_id, no role — the session is
   pinned to the api-key's bot user / admin tenant.
   NOTE: a **service-account OTP login**
   (`grant_type=otp` resolving a `kind=service` user,
   ADR-071) is *user-shaped*: it returns
   `subject_type:"service"` **with** tenants[] / tenant_id /
   role / user — shapes 1/2 with `subject_type:"service"`.

**MFA is NOT signalled here.** There is no
`status:"mfa_required"` login shape — every successful
credential exchange returns `status:"ok"` **including a
refresh token** even when MFA is still pending. An
MFA-requiring membership is flagged per-tenant via
`tenants[].mfa_required` (which suppresses the shape-1
access-token fast path), and the `412 mfa_required`
precondition (`PreconditionMFA`) is raised later, on the
`POST /auth/token` tenant mint.

LoginResponseM2M.description:
Api-key (M2M) login — pinned to the api-key's bot user + admin
tenant. `tenants` is present but **always `[]`** on this shape;
`tenant_id` / `role` / `user` are omitted (those are user
concepts). Emitted by `grant_type=api_key` / `platform_api_key`
only — a service-account **OTP** login is user-shaped (see
`LoginResponse` shape 3 note).

idle_ttl.description: Zone idle-timeout duration (seconds); see LoginResponseUserResolved.idle_ttl. Absent / 0 = disabled. Optional.

refresh_exp.description: Absolute refresh-token expiry (unix seconds); see LoginResponseUserResolved.refresh_exp. Optional.

tenants.description: Always the empty array on api-key grants.

LoginResponseUserMultiTenant.description:
Multi-tenant user — or a single-tenant user whose membership has
`mfa_required:true` (the access-token fast path is suppressed).
Caller must pick a tenant and call `/auth/token` with the
refresh + `tenant_id` (which raises `412 mfa_required` when MFA
is still unsatisfied for that tenant).

user.description: The resolved subject's user id (see LoginResponseUserResolved.user).

LoginResponseUserResolved.description:
Single-tenant user, no MFA pending — fully resolved on the first
call. `subject_type` is `service` (not `user`) when the resolved
subject is a `kind=service` account (`grant_type=otp`, ADR-071).

`revoked_sids` (ADR-104 R-e) is present ONLY when this sign-in changed a
`must_change` password (R15): exactly the session ids that change ended
across the person's whole identity in the zone (`[]` when none; only
what was actually ended on `anchor_only`). The new session is not listed.

idle_ttl.description: Zone-configured idle (inactivity) session timeout, in seconds — a sliding-window DURATION (resets on each request), NOT an absolute expiry (ADR-070). The BFF force-logs-out a session idle for longer than this; the issuer only reports the value. Absent / 0 = idle timeout disabled for this zone (the default). Sourced straight from `zones.config.idle_ttl_seconds` with no min-of-three compute.

refresh_exp.description: Absolute wall-clock expiry (unix seconds) of the refresh token — the min of the rolling refresh TTL, the ADR-054 scheduled cutoff, and the ADR-058 absolute session cap. Distinct from `expires_in` (the access-token lifetime, in seconds). Optional and forward-compatible: absent on pre-refresh_exp issuers, so a consumer sizing a session from it must fall back to its own ceiling when absent/zero.

tenant_choice_required.description:
ADR-092 D5. The caller holds two or more ACTIVE memberships in a zone whose `single_tenant_membership` is on, and must settle the picker via POST /me/tenant-choice. Optional; omitted when false.
This login SUCCEEDED — an access token is still issued, and the field is a reconciliation prompt, not an authentication failure. Treating it as an auth error would strand exactly the users the drain exists to resolve, leaving them no credential to answer with.

tenant_choices.description: ADR-092 D5. The memberships the picker may choose between; present only alongside `tenant_choice_required`. The chosen membership is KEPT and the others are suspended (recoverable) with their sessions revoked.

is_owner.description: This membership CANNOT be given up — `tenants.owner_user_id` is NOT NULL, so revoking it would leave the tenant ownerless. The server refuses such a choice with 409 `owner_cannot_be_revoked`; clients should not offer it, and must still handle the refusal since the client is not the authority.

user.description:
The resolved subject's user id. Present on every user-grant
login (even when no access token is minted) so a BFF can
resolve the user without decoding the JWT `sub`. Omitted on
api-key (M2M) grants.

all.description:
`true` revokes EVERY session of the identity in the zone, including
sessions anchored on a sibling org's membership (the same scope as
`DELETE /auth/sessions`; ADR-109 D11 amendment, 2026-10-02), and
the response's `revoked_sids` names exactly those sessions. If the
identity's memberships cannot be resolved the call fails and
nothing is revoked.

revoked_sids.description:
ADR-109 D11 (Q5). Present only when the request had `all: true`:
every session id revoked by the call, the presenting session
included.

sid.description:
ADR-109 D11 (from Issuer A; DESIGNED, NOT BUILT). The revoked
session's id (`sessions.jti`), equal to the `sid` claim of its
access tokens. Absent from an issuer older than Issuer A; a client
then falls back to a non-expired access token's `sid`/`jti`.

PreconditionFirstLoginPending.description:
412 response when the first login on a recently-vacated contact
slot (slot_recycled_until > now; ADR-042 P2) is held for tenant-
owner approval. The IdP proof is stashed as a pending
contact_verification (verification_id); login returns no session.
The owner approves/rejects via
POST /tenants/{id}/contact-verifications/{cvId}/approve|reject,
after which the user re-logs in.

PreconditionMFA.description: 412 response when target tenant requires MFA.

PreconditionSessionLimit.description:
412 response when concurrent session cap is hit at login.
Extends the base {code, message} error envelope with the
short-lived revocation_token (scope: session:list + session:revoke,
TTL = zone challenge TTL) and the list of active sessions the UI
shows in the Session-Limit modal. See TEST_INVENTORY §2.6.

device_name.description: Human-readable label for the device that created this session (e.g. a CLI hostname), supplied at login via the `X-Device-Name` header. Omitted when the session carries no label. Lets a user tell sessions apart when revoking (ADR-062).

mfa_methods.description:
The MFA methods this membership must satisfy (union of the
user's enrollment and the role/zone requirements —
`computeMFAMethods`, ADR-059/075). Empty/omitted when no
method-specific requirement applies.

role.description:
The user's role in this tenant. Any name from the zone's
role catalog (`GET /platforms/{id}/roles`): the system roles
`owner` / `admin` / `member` / `viewer` / `platform_api`, or
a platform-defined custom role (ADR-040). Not a closed enum.

TokenRequest.description:
Refresh-token rotation. The body's `tenant_id` is **required
only** when selecting a tenant for a multi-tenant user
(response shape #2 from `/auth/login`). For service /
platform refresh tokens, `tenant_id` is **ignored** — those
sessions are pinned to the api-key's admin tenant.

custom_claims.description:
Optional partner-supplied claims, gated by
`zones.config.access_token_custom_claim_keys`
(SDK SPEC §4.2).

A key that collides with a reserved JWT claim name is now
**refused** with 400 `reserved_claim_key`, not dropped
(ADR-097 D3). A dropped claim is indistinguishable, from your
side, from an honoured one — and once `scope` carries granted
authority, that difference is a gate that never fires.

product_roles.description:
**ADR-102 — the PARTNER's role NAME, carried and never read.**

`scope` carries *authority*; this carries the *name of the role*
the bearer holds in YOUR system, for display ("Signed in as:
Dispatch"), routing, report defaults and your own audit trail.
The two ride the same token and answer different questions.

⚠️ **Do not branch AUTHORIZATION on this claim.** A name is a
label, a scope is a grant. Keying authorization off the name
re-creates exactly the coupling ADR-101 spent four migrations
removing — add a role and every service needs editing. Use
`scope`.

**Distinct from `role`**, which is ZoneID's OWN vocabulary and is
a trusted authorization lookup key on the direct-bearer lane. The
two claims are never merged and this one reaches no ZoneID gate;
a test asserts the claim name appears nowhere in the issuer's
authorization surface.

**Validated for SHAPE ONLY**, then written onto the token
verbatim. Nothing is stored, compared against a catalog, or
intersected. An ARRAY, not a space-delimited string: partner role
names are not constrained to the RFC 6749 §3.3 scope charset, and
a legitimate `"Regional Manager"` must survive.

**Bounds are CONSTANTS, not zone config**: at most **16**
elements of at most **64 bytes** each — `too_many_product_roles`
/ `product_role_too_long`. Each element must be non-empty, valid
UTF-8 and free of control characters (`invalid_product_role`).
Deliberately NOT the `user_api_keys.max_permission_strings` knobs,
which already govern two unrelated things.

**Re-resolved on every mint, never stored on the session.** Send
it each time. Omitting it mints no `product_roles` at all — an
absent claim and an empty array mean the same thing, which is why
an empty array mints nothing rather than `[]`.

**Reserved**: it cannot be forged through `custom_claims`
(`reserved_claim_key`).

**`/auth/token` only** — `POST /auth/login` does not accept it, so
the token login returns carries no `product_roles`. The ZoneID
SDKs close that gap for you: `Login` follows the login with a
`/auth/token` mint once the tenant is settled (ADR-102 D10).

refresh_token.description: Optional — refresh may also arrive via Authorization header.

role_permissions.description:
**ADR-100 D16 — the narrowing operand for a user-API-key token.**
The permissions the holder's ROLE confers, in YOUR vocabulary, used
to narrow that token's `permissions_cap` claim to THIS org — on REFRESH as well as login (D18).

Supply it on EVERY mint. A user-API-key session IS refreshable —
the key row is re-read here too — so a refresh that omitted this
would hand back a token WIDER than the one it replaced, silently and
on a schedule.

Supply it from your own role -> permission map. ZoneID stores no
partner catalog and will not resolve it for you (D17): the strings
are opaque here, and the issuer does not fall back to
`zone_roles.permissions` even for `aud=zoneid`, so the claim stays

subset of `A` for every `B`, so a wrong or hostile list can only

pre-ADR-100 behaviour.

**OPTIONAL. Omitted / `null` = not supplied** — the stored cap
travels unnarrowed (D6), which keeps every existing caller working.
**An empty array is NOT the same thing**: it says "this role confers
nothing here" and produces a `403` (below).

**Ignored for an UNCAPPED key** (D7), whose claim stays absent
whatever you send — uncapped is delivered by omission and that
mechanism does not change. Ignored, too, for any token that is not
key-derived: there is no cap to intersect with.

⚠️ **An empty INTERSECTION is `403 no_permissions_in_org`, never an
empty claim** (D8). The two are indistinguishable to a reader of the
token, and `[]` on the claim side already means "capped to nothing",

names the org, or it reads as "the key is broken".

scope.description:
**ADR-097 §A — granted authority, space-delimited.**

RFC 9068 §2.2.3, which defines the claim by reference to RFC
8693 §4.2 ("a JSON string containing a space-separated list of
scopes") in RFC 6749 §3.3 format. A STRING, not an array.

These are **your** scope strings. ZoneID stores no partner
catalog: the values are never parsed, validated against a
vocabulary, persisted, or interpreted. Your repo owns the
route -> scope and role -> scope maps; the ZoneID SDK is the
gate that evaluates them.

**Charset (RFC 6749 §3.3):** `%x21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E` —
printable ASCII minus SPACE, `"` and `\`. Case-SENSITIVE, no
normalization. A space inside a value would split one scope into
two, so a malformed entry is refused at mint (`invalid_scope`)
rather than silently reshaped.

**Bounded** by the zone's `user_api_keys.max_permission_strings`
and `max_permission_string_len` (defaults 32 / 128) —
`too_many_scopes` / `scope_too_long`. The same knobs, not a
second vocabulary for the same kind of string.

**Intersected server-side.** When the session came from a user
API key, the minted claim is `scope` INTERSECTED with the key's
live `permissions_cap` — exact string match, no wildcards, no
hierarchy. ZoneID does this so that a caller who bypasses the
SDK still receives a narrowed token.

**Re-resolved on every call.** The claim is never stored on the
session: send it each time. Omitting it mints no `scope` at all.

**Revocation lag.** A token-carried scope is only as fresh as
the token: revoking a grant takes effect within
`access_ttl_seconds`. Where a stale grant is unacceptable —
money movement, permission administration, data export — use the
SDK's `CapAllows`, which reads live and has zero lag.

Not accepted on a service-class refresh (`scope_not_supported`).

tenant_id.description:
Required for multi-tenant user pick. Ignored when the
refresh token's `subject_type` is `service` or
`platform`.

TokenResponse.description:
Access + rotated-refresh response. `tenant_id` and `role`
are present only when `subject_type=user`; absent for
`service` refresh. ADR-089: a credential-bootstrapped
session (api key / WIF) has NO refresh token, so this
endpoint serves only users and ADR-071 service accounts.
`refresh_token` is rotated unconditionally for users; for
a service account only when the zone has opted in via
`service_refresh_rotates` (otherwise the same refresh is
echoed back unchanged).

idle_ttl.description: Zone idle-timeout duration (seconds); see LoginResponseUserResolved.idle_ttl. Absent / 0 = disabled. Optional.

refresh_exp.description: Absolute expiry (unix seconds) of the rotated refresh token (or, when rotation is off for a service/platform refresh, of the unchanged echoed token); see LoginResponseUserResolved.refresh_exp. Optional.

post.description:
ADR-051 (v0.7.0). Single credential-exchange endpoint. The
body's `grant_type` selects the credential exchange and the
subject class of the issued tokens. See `LoginRequest` for
the per-grant fields and inbound bearer rules. The legacy
`method` alias is removed (sunset 2026-08-01) — a body without
`grant_type` 400s `missing_grant_type`.

Inbound bearer:
- **User grants** (`provider_token`, `password`,
  `otp`) require `Authorization: Bearer <platform
  access token>`. `password` is implemented (ADR-104) and
  answers `400 unknown_method` only when the deployment has no
  credential store or the zone's `password_login_enabled` is off.
  (This line said "reserved, not implemented" until spec `0.53.0`;
  that was stale since ADR-104 shipped.) The zone is resolved from the bearer's
  `zone_id` claim; body `zone_id` is ignored. ADR-046
  `aud` validation still applies on `provider_token` /
  `google`.
- **Api-key grants** (`api_key`, `platform_api_key`) carry
  the raw key in the body and reject any inbound bearer.

ADR-051 hard cut: `POST /auth/service-token` and
`POST /auth/platform-token` are deleted in v0.7.0; both URLs
return 404. Migrate to this endpoint with
`grant_type: api_key` / `grant_type: platform_api_key`.

parameters.description: Optional human-readable device label persisted on the created session and surfaced in GET /auth/sessions (ADR-062). Control characters are stripped and the value is capped at 120 chars. Only the user grants record it.
parameters.name: X-Device-Name

200.description:
OK — every successful credential exchange returns
`status:"ok"` **including a refresh token even when MFA is
still pending** (MFA is flagged per-tenant via
`tenants[].mfa_required`; the `412 mfa_required`
precondition is raised later, on `POST /auth/token`).

400.description:
bad_json (malformed body)
| missing_grant_type (no `grant_type`; the legacy `method`
alias was removed at its 2026-08-01 sunset)
| bad_grant_type (unrecognised `grant_type`)
| missing_provider (`grant_type=provider_token` without
`provider`)
| unknown_method (provider/method not enabled for the zone;
for `grant_type=password`: no credential store, or the zone's
`password_login_enabled` is off)
| tenant_required (`grant_type=password` with a username and no
tenant from `tenant_id` or the request's host; ADR-104 D2)
| password_too_short | password_too_long | password_unchanged
(`new_password` failed input validation; ADR-104 R14)
| password_change_not_required (`new_password` sent for a
credential that is not must-change; ADR-104 R17)
| bad_tenant_id (`tenant_id` not in the resolved zone)
| missing_api_key (api-key grants without `api_key`)
| missing_subject_token | bad_subject_token_type
(token-exchange grant, ADR-057).

401.description:
unauthorized (missing or invalid platform token; user
grants only)
| wrong_scope (bearer is not `token_class=platform`; the
error CODE is unchanged, only the claim it reads)
| invalid_audience (id-token `aud` not registered;
`provider_token` / `google`)
| invalid_credentials (bad password / OTP / api-key)
| key_class_mismatch (declared `grant_type` doesn't
match the api-key's class — `api_key` vs
`platform_api_key`; ADR-051)
| revoked_api_key (api-key grants; key soft-revoked)
| keyless_api_key (api-key not bound to a bot user).

403.description:
user_not_invited (known user, no membership in the resolved
zone) | signup_domain_not_allowed | user_suspended |
no_permissions_in_org | password_must_change.

`password_must_change` is ADR-104 D7: the password was CORRECT but
an administrator set it. Resend the same body with `new_password`
(see `LoginRequestPassword`) to replace it and sign in in one call.

`no_permissions_in_org` is ADR-100 D8: on `grant_type=user_api_key`,
the key's `permissions_cap` and the supplied `role_permissions` have
nothing in common IN THIS ORG, so there is no authority to mint. It
is a refusal rather than a token with an empty claim, because the
two are indistinguishable to a reader of the token. The message
NAMES the org — the narrowing is per-org, so the identical request
succeeds against a different `tenant_id`.
(A `zone_mismatch` 403 was previously documented here but
is not emitted by this handler.)

412.description:
session_limit_reached (concurrent session cap hit) |
first_login_pending_approval (first login on a recently-
vacated contact slot awaits tenant-owner approval; ADR-042 P2).
NOTE: `mfa_required` is NOT raised here — see the 200
description and `POST /auth/token`.

429.description:
login_throttled — `grant_type=password` only: the per-identifier
fail counter (keyed on zone + identifier as supplied, consulted
before any lookup) is locked. A correct password, and a valid
`new_password`, are refused alike and nothing changes.

501.description:
federation_disabled (token-exchange grant while workload
identity federation is not enabled; ADR-057)

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a refresh (+ access if resolved)

post.description:
Resolves the session from the refresh token (body `refresh_token`, or
the bearer when the body has none) and revokes it; with `all: true`,
every session of that session's user. An unknown or already-spent
refresh token is `401`.

From ADR-109 Issuer A (DESIGNED, NOT BUILT) the `200` body also carries
`sid`: the id of the session the presented refresh token belonged to,
the same value as the `sid` claim on that session's access tokens. An
SDK revokes that `sid` in its own session store, so logout is keyed by
the refresh-token holder rather than by any access token. With
`all: true` it is still only the presenting session's id.
post.summary: Revoke the current session (or all sessions)

post.description:
Accepts a refresh token (Bearer header or body) and returns
a fresh access token plus a (possibly rotated) refresh token.
Works for all three subject classes — the response carries
`subject_type ∈ {user, service, platform}`.

Body `tenant_id` is required only when the refresh token's
subject is a multi-tenant **user** (response shape #2 from
`/auth/login`). For service / platform refresh tokens
`tenant_id` is **ignored** — those sessions are pinned to
the api-key's bot user / admin tenant.

Rotation policy (ADR-051): user refresh tokens always
rotate (ADR-031 reuse-detection). An ADR-071 service-account
refresh token rotates only when the zone has opted in via
`service_refresh_rotates`; otherwise the same refresh is
echoed back unchanged. ADR-089: a credential-bootstrapped
session (`grant_type` ∈ {`api_key`, `platform_api_key`,
token-exchange}) has no refresh token — presenting one
returns `401 m2m_refresh_withdrawn`; re-mint via
`POST /auth/login` instead.

**BFF gate (ADR-041).** When the refresh-bound session's zone
is not the base zone, this endpoint requires a partner
platform bearer in `Authorization` and the refresh token MUST be
supplied in the **body** (the header is the platform JWT, not the
refresh). The zone is resolved from the refresh-bound session, so
the gate applies to **every** refresh class — user, service, and
platform — not just tenant-scoped user refreshes. A missing/invalid
platform bearer returns `401 bff_bearer_required`.

Returns 412 if the tenant's MFA policy requires a challenge
the caller has not completed.

400.description:
missing_tenant_id (refresh subject is a multi-tenant user and
the body carries no `tenant_id`) | bad_request (a
`custom_claims` key is not in the zone's
`access_token_custom_claim_keys` allowlist)
| reserved_claim_key (a `custom_claims` key is a reserved JWT
claim name — ADR-097 D3; previously dropped silently)
| invalid_scope (a `scope` entry is not an RFC 6749 §3.3
scope-token)
| too_many_scopes / scope_too_long (`scope` exceeds the zone's
`user_api_keys.max_permission_strings` /
`max_permission_string_len`)
| scope_not_supported (this session class mints no `scope`)
| bad_json.

403.description:
not_a_member | user_suspended | no_permissions_in_org. The last is
ADR-100 D8, identical to `/auth/login`'s: it exists on BOTH routes
or the narrowing is only enforced at login, since a session
bootstrapped from a user API key is refreshable and a token that
could not be minted at login could otherwise be obtained by
refreshing an older one.

NOTE: a **deactivated** user
also returns `user_suspended` — the previously-documented
separate `deactivated` code is collapsed into
`user_suspended` (suspended and deactivated map to the same
error in `authsvc`).

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token into a new refresh + access pair
